facts.claim: Lighter Flotilla sells goods and services to travellers.
A traveller can rest safely at Lighter Flotilla.
The people of Lighter Flotilla are caught in a quarrel the player can see.
Lighter Flotilla offers services to travellers.
A player can buy and sell at Lighter Flotilla.
Lighter Flotilla gives shelter for the night.
The lighter crews live aboard their boats at permanent moorings beside the lighter quay.
The crews lighter goods ashore from the large ships that cannot dock at Lilmoth.
The moorings lie in sheltered estuary water off Lilmoth's east bank.
A council attempt to license lightering caused a two-week stoppage.
A line of masts stands along the south side of the pier.
The tall trade ship lies alongside the pier head.
Some hulls have their sails furled on the yards.
Plank ferries are moored singly along the north side of the pier.
A short landing stage runs over the reed shallows to the pier foot.
Five working hulls are moored as houses along one timber pier.
The Alten Meerhleel trade ship lies alongside the pier head.
A lighter lies alongside the pier's north side.
The crews who move every cargo in the bay live aboard these hulls.
The player can carry the licensing offer between the council and the crews.
A hidden cache holds cargo landed off a hull that never reached the quay.
From the bank the flotilla looks like a moored fleet.
A timber pier runs between the bows and the market rafts.
Every hull is afloat and in use.
Few of the hulls would pass a sea survey.
The moorings have not shifted in years.
The mood is independent and orderly.
The colours are tarred hulls, pale furled canvas and brown estuary water.
Gangplanks and gear knock all night, and rigging creaks.
Crews cook on deck.
The air smells of tar, bilge and estuary.
The lighter crews control the link between deep-water hulls and the city.
The crews know what that link is worth.
A dredged deep-water channel would end the flotilla.
The channel would also end the city's hold on its own trade.
